To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mass distributions of the Δ0 and Δ ++ resonances produced in CTa collisions are similar to the analogous distributions of Δ0- or Δ ++-resonance masses produced in the π−12C, 4HeC, and CC reactions.
the mass distributions of the Δ0 and Δ+ + resonances produced in CTa interactions are reconstructed for the first time.
the production of Δ isobars on Ta nuclei in CTa interactions at a projectile energy of 4.21 GeV per nucleon is observed for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of Δ0-Δ++ isobars produced on tantalum nuclei at a projectile momentum 4.2GeV/c per nucleon.
the study of the properties of Δ0 andΔ++ resonances produced by CTa interactions.

the production of Δ isobars in CTa collisions, the parameters of the Δ0 and Δ+ + resonances produced in such interactions were obtained for the first time, and the contribution of the Δ0- and the Δ+ + -resonance decaying to charged pion production was estimated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Δ0 and Δ+ + isobar parameters obtained from CTa and CC interactions are similar, while the Δ0 andΔ++ parameters obtained in CTa and π−12C reactions differ.
the Δ0 and Δ+ resonances were not observed in the CTa interaction at the projectile momentum of 1.2 GeV per nucleon.
the Δ0 and Δ+ resonances were produced on the target nucleons with the same probability in all the studied reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of Δ resonances on nuclei in the momentum range 4-40 GeV/c per nucleus is a complex process that is determined by the properties of the target nucleus and the projectile momentum.

the production of Δ-isobar resonances in collisions of 4.5 GeV/c per-nucleon carbon ions with tantalum nuclei is more efficient than in π−12 C collisions at 40 GeV and in CC and 12C4 He collisions at 4.2GeV/c per nucleon, and the production of Δ-resonances in CTa collisions is more efficient than that in CC and 42C4 He collisions, while the production of Δ+ in CC and
the Δ0 resonance is produced more abundantly in CTa interactions than in the analogous CC and π−12C processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Δ0 and Δ+-isobar production mechanisms on CTa and C targets are identical.

Δ0 and Δ+-resonance production in CTa interactions at a projectile energy of 4.4 GeV per nucleon is comparable with the Δ0 and Δ±-resonance production observed in π−12 C interactions at a projectile velocity of 0.8c.
the procedure for reconstructing the mass distributions of resonances can be successfully used for the study of Δ isobars on heavy nuclei.
